name: Toyota RAV4
title: Toyota RAV4 Problems by Year: Years to Avoid and What Owners Report | Steer Me Right
description: Which Toyota RAV4 model years to buy used and which to skip, from NHTSA owner complaints per 100,000 sold, recalls by year, and what owners report on Reddit.
h1: Toyota RAV4 problems by year: years to avoid and what owners report
card: Which RAV4 model years to buy used and which to skip, with NHTSA complaints per 100,000 sold, recalls by year and what owners report.
answer: The best used RAV4s are the 2022 to 2025 model years, which draw {r:2022}, {r:2023}, {r:2024} and {r:2025} NHTSA owner complaints per 100,000 sold. Skip the 2019 and 2020: they draw {r:2019} and {r:2020}, led by fuel-system, engine and steering complaints, and Toyota recalled them for engine casting cracks, lost steering assist and cracked front control arms. A 2021 is worth a look only if both of its air bag recalls are done, and the 2016 to 2018 RAV4s sit in the middle.

The rates divide each model year’s NHTSA complaints, counted across every RAV4 listing (gas, Hybrid and Prime or Plug-in Hybrid), by U.S. sales. They compare years with each other; they don’t predict one car. The 2026 redesign is too new to rate; our RAV4 price guide covers what it costs new.
salesNote: Sales come from Toyota’s year-end releases for 2019 to 2025 and Good Car Bad Car for 2016 to 2018.

2016: {r:2016} per 100,000. Electrical ({k:2016:ELECTRICAL SYSTEM}) and brakes ({k:2016:SERVICE BRAKES}) lead the complaints. Recall 23V-734 covers replacement batteries that may not fit the tray.
2017: Electrical leads again with {k:2017:ELECTRICAL SYSTEM} of {c:2017} complaints, and the battery-tray recall 23V-734 applies.
2018: Electrical has {k:2018:ELECTRICAL SYSTEM} of {c:2018} complaints. The last year of the old design, and recall 23V-734 applies.
2019: {r:2019} per 100,000 against {r:2022} for the 2022. Fuel and hybrid system ({k:2019:FUEL/PROPULSION SYSTEM}) and engine ({k:2019:ENGINE}) lead, and {rec:2019} recalls include engine casting cracks (20V-064), steering assist (20V-373) and front control arms (20V-286).
2020: {r:2020} per 100,000, led by engine ({k:2020:ENGINE}). The same three recalls as 2019 apply, plus 20V-734 for the steering column’s air bag pins.
2021: {r:2021} per 100,000, but {k:2021:AIR BAGS} of {c:2021} complaints name air bags, and two free recalls cover them (20V-734, 23V-865). Buy only with both done.
avoid to check: the complaint spike traces to recalls a VIN lookup confirms
2022: {r:2022} per 100,000, the lowest of the 2019 to 2022 years. Recalls include the front passenger seat sensor (22V-519).
2023: {r:2023} per 100,000. Electrical ({k:2023:ELECTRICAL SYSTEM}) and steering ({k:2023:STEERING}) lead. An instrument cluster recall (25V-595) covers 2023 to 2025.
2024: {r:2024} per 100,000. Recall 24V-911 covers loose front brake caliper bolts; ask that it was done.
2025: {r:2025} per 100,000, and the count is still growing as the year ages. Recall 26V-256 covers front seat bracket welds.
2026: {c:2026} complaints so far and no full year of sales. The plug-in has recall 26V-659 (power loss at higher speeds): get its software update before delivery.

generations.name: Fourth generation
generations.text: The 2016 refresh added LED lamps and a color display, and the RAV4 Hybrid debuted with it (Wikipedia). The 2016 to 2018 years on this page are the last of that design, with the 2.5-liter four-cylinder and six-speed automatic as the core powertrain.

generations.name: Fifth generation
generations.text: It went on sale in December 2018 with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder and an eight-speed automatic; the Hybrid, with standard all-wheel drive, followed in March 2019 (Wikipedia). The RAV4 Prime plug-in arrived for 2021 and was renamed Plug-in Hybrid for 2025. A refresh for 2022 brought new headlights and USB-C ports, the Woodland trim arrived for 2023, and the Adventure and TRD Off-Road trims were dropped for 2025.

generations.name: Sixth generation
generations.text: Toyota sells the redesigned 2026 only as a hybrid or plug-in hybrid, so the gas engine that carried the 2019 to 2025 cars is gone (Wikipedia; Toyota’s 2026 RAV4 page). Its record is too short to compare with the figures above.

problems.title: Fuel and hybrid system
problems.text: CarComplaints reports that some hybrids’ fuel tanks won’t fill to the rated 14.5 gallons, and that a settlement extended that coverage to 15 years or 150,000 miles. NHTSA’s fuel label also catches complaints about gas models, so this count is wider than that one issue.

problems.title: Engine
problems.text: Recall 20V-064 covers porosity in 2.5-liter engine castings that can crack and leak coolant. The fix is free and can mean a replacement engine. Ask for proof it was done on any 2019 or 2020.

problems.title: Air bags
problems.text: Two recalls: 20V-734 (steering column breakaway pins that can affect the driver air bag) and 23V-865 (a short circuit in the passenger occupant sensor that can stop the passenger air bag firing). Both are free; a VIN lookup shows whether they are open.

problems.title: Electrical system
problems.text: NHTSA’s complaint field names the part, not the failure. For 2016 to 2018, one recall (23V-734) covers replacement 12-volt batteries that don’t fit the tray, and NHTSA’s closed investigation PE21005 traced battery-area fires on 2013 to 2018 RAV4s to that fit.

problems.title: Steering
problems.text: The counts are small beside 2019 and 2020. Recall 20V-373 (water in the steering gearbox, lost assist) covers only 2019 and 2020, so nothing in NHTSA’s recall list explains these; check the steering on any 2022 to 2025 you drive.

paragraphs: Reddit’s reliability gripes are water leaking in from roof rails or clogged drains, a coolant valve message, and worry over salt on the hybrid’s exposed high-voltage cable. The threads rarely give a model year, so Reddit neither confirms nor contradicts the year-by-year table.

notableRecalls.title: Engine casting cracks
notableRecalls.text: Porosity in 2.5-liter engine castings can crack and leak coolant, which can overheat the engine. Dealers inspect and replace the engine as needed, free.

notableRecalls.title: Steering assist loss
notableRecalls.text: Water can enter the electric steering gearbox cover and cut power assist. Dealers replace the gearbox, free.

notableRecalls.title: Front control arm cracks
notableRecalls.text: The front lower suspension arms may crack and separate from the wheel assembly. Dealers replace both arms, free.

notableRecalls.title: Air bag recalls
notableRecalls.text: 20V-734 covers steering column breakaway pins that can affect the driver air bag, and 23V-865 a short in the passenger occupant sensor. Both fixes are free.

notableRecalls.title: Plug-in charger fire risk
notableRecalls.text: A damaged DC-DC converter module can short and overheat. Until the dealer replaces it, Toyota tells owners not to charge below about 41 degrees Fahrenheit.

notableRecalls.title: Brake caliper bolts
notableRecalls.text: Front caliper and wheel-bearing bolts may be loose, which can damage the brake hose or detach a wheel. Dealers inspect and tighten them, free.

notableRecalls.title: Front seat brackets
notableRecalls.text: Seat rail brackets may be welded improperly. Dealers inspect and repair the welds, free.

notableRecalls.title: Power loss at higher speeds
notableRecalls.text: A software error can cut power or shut the plug-in system down at higher speeds. Dealers update the software, free; owner letters begin November 22, 2026.

noInvestigations: NHTSA’s public investigation list showed no open investigation naming the RAV4 on November 21, 2026. The last, PE21005 into battery-area fires on 2013 to 2018 RAV4s, closed in August 2024 after Toyota’s battery-tray recall 23V-734.

checks.title: Hybrid cables on 2019 to 2022 AWD hybrids.
checks.text: Toyota’s support program 22TE09 covers corroded high-voltage cables for 8 years or 100,000 miles. It isn’t a recall, so a VIN lookup won’t show it; ask for the service record.

checks.title: The 2019 and 2020 recalls.
checks.text: Confirm 20V-064 (engine), 20V-373 (steering) and 20V-286 (control arms) are closed on the VIN. A dealer can print the history.

checks.title: The fuel tank on a 2019 to 2021 hybrid.
checks.text: Owners report hybrids that stop filling well short of the rated 14.5 gallons. Ask what the seller’s last fill-up took.

checks.title: A plug-in’s charger and software.
checks.text: On a 2021 or 2022 Prime, confirm the DC-DC converter recall (23V-478); on a 2026, the software recall 26V-659.

checks.title: Damp carpet and headliner.
checks.text: Owners on Reddit report water leaking in from roof rails or clogged drains. Press the carpet under the seats and look for stains at the roof edges.

checks.title: An independent inspection.
checks.text: Have a shop that isn’t the seller’s look over the brakes, steering and underbody before you sign.

newer: Toyota sells the 2026 only as a hybrid or plug-in hybrid, so the 2019 to 2025 gas engine’s record doesn’t carry over. With {c:2026} complaints, {rec:2026} recalls and no full year on the road, it is too early to say it is more reliable; the plug-in needs its recall 26V-659 software update.
If you are choosing between a new 2026 and a used 2022 to 2025, our RAV4 price guide has the new prices, the discount to aim for and our take on buying new.
faq: What are the worst Toyota RAV4 years?

The 2019 and 2020 model years. They draw {r:2019} and {r:2020} NHTSA complaints per 100,000 sold against {r:2022} to {r:2025} for 2022 to 2025, and carry recalls for engine casting cracks, steering assist loss and front control arm cracks.
What is the best used RAV4 year?
The 2022 to 2025 model years have the lowest complaint rates, from {r:2025} for the 2025 to {r:2023} for the 2023. The 2025 is still collecting complaints, so its rate will rise a little.
It draws {r:2021} complaints per 100,000, but {k:2021:AIR BAGS} of its {c:2021} complaints name air bags, and two free recalls cover those. We’d buy one with both recalls shown as done.
Do RAV4 hybrids have more problems than the gas model?
NHTSA counts them together here, so these figures can’t split them. The hybrid-specific items are the 2019 to 2022 AWD cable program 22TE09 and the fuel tank fill complaints on 2019 to 2021 hybrids.
How do I check a used RAV4 for recalls?
Enter the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. It lists open recalls for that car; recall repairs are free at a Toyota dealer.
